card.statement: For a finite poset ${\cal P}=\{p_1,\dots,p_t\}$, we study systems $(U_1,\dots,U_t)_U$ of subspaces $U_1,\dots,U_t$ of a unitary space $U$ such that $U_i\subseteq U_j$ if $p_i\prec p_j$. Two systems $(U_1,\dots,U_t)_U$ and $(V_1,\dots,V_t)_V$ are said to be isometric if there exists an isometry $\varphi:U\to V$ such that $\varphi(U_i)=V_i$. We classify such systems up to isometry if $\cal P$ is a semichain. We prove that the problem of their classification is unitarily wild if $\cal P$ is not a semichain. A classification problem is called unitarily wild if it contains the problem of classifying linear operators on a unitary space, which is hopeless in a certain sense.
card.label: Abstract

paper.title: Systems of subspaces of a unitary space
paper.abstract: For a given poset, we consider its representations by systems of subspaces of a unitary space ordered by inclusion. We classify such systems for all posets for which an explicit classification is possible.
